label: Apple
detail: Name a Legacy Contact and share the access key.
doNow: Open Settings › your name › Sign-In & Security › Legacy Contact.
Add the contact, share or print the access key, and confirm they received it.
later: Open Apple Digital Legacy and submit the access key plus death certificate.
Follow any additional regional legal-document request from Apple.
boundary: Apple does not release iCloud Keychain passwords, passkeys or payment information, and purchased media does not transfer through Legacy Contact.

label: Google
detail: Choose inactivity timing, contacts, data and deletion.
doNow: Open Inactive Account Manager and choose the inactivity period.
Select up to ten contacts, the data each may receive, and whether to delete the account.
later: Use Google’s deceased-user form for closure, funds or selected content.
Request content before closure; closing the account can prevent a later content request.
requirements: Death and relationship or authority evidence
boundary: Inactivity is not proof of death. Google never gives out passwords, and every deceased-user request is reviewed.
links: Request help for a deceased user

label: Facebook & Instagram
detail: Set Facebook memorialization; keep Instagram’s request route.
doNow: In Facebook Accounts Centre, open Account ownership and control › Memorialisation.
Choose a Legacy Contact or Delete after death; record the Instagram profile separately.
later: Use Facebook’s memorialization or removal process.
Use Instagram’s separate deceased-account form; never sign in as the deceased person.
requirements: Relationship or estate authority for removal
boundary: A Facebook Legacy Contact cannot log in or read messages. Instagram does not publish the same Legacy Contact setting.

label: GitHub
detail: Invite a repository successor before access is needed.
doNow: Invite another GitHub user and confirm they accepted.
later: The successor or authorized person contacts GitHub Support and states the requested action.
Provide the username, relationship and requested identity, death or authority documents.
boundary: A successor cannot sign in as the user and can manage only the public user-owned repository scope described by GitHub.

label: Password managers
detail: Use the provider’s recovery or emergency-access design.
doNow: For Bitwarden, invite and confirm an Emergency Access contact and wait period.
For 1Password Families, add another organizer, save the Emergency Kit and generate a recovery code.
later: Bitwarden uses an approved or delayed emergency-access request.
1Password organizer recovery is account recovery, not a legal estate decision.
boundary: Emergency access can expose highly sensitive vault data and does not create legal authority. Never store a vault master password, Secret Key or recovery code in Rillora.

label: Microsoft
detail: Outlook and OneDrive access depends on region and law.
doNow: Record the account identifier and billing locator; Microsoft does not publish a consumer Legacy Contact setting.
later: Use Microsoft’s deceased-account instructions for the account region.
Expect a court-order route for content in many regions; China and Germany have documented alternatives.
requirements: Court order or region-specific authority documents
boundary: A request does not guarantee account content. Requirements vary materially by region.

label: LinkedIn
detail: Memorialize the profile or request closure with authority.
doNow: Record the profile URL, account email and preferred memorialize-or-close outcome.
later: Report the death for memorialization, or request closure if legally authorized.
Submit the profile, death information and LinkedIn-accepted court authority documents.
boundary: LinkedIn never provides usernames or passwords. Memorialization locks access.

label: X
detail: An estate representative or close family member can request deactivation.
doNow: Record the handle, profile URL and preferred outcome; do not plan around another person receiving access.
later: Submit X’s removal request, then follow the emailed identity and death-certificate instructions.
requirements: Estate authority or verified family relationship
boundary: X’s published route deactivates the account. It does not give another person account access.
links: Contact X about a deceased user

label: PayPal
detail: An executor can request closure and balance handling.
doNow: Record the primary email and exact PayPal country/entity without storing a payment credential.
later: The executor follows PayPal’s regional deceased-account process.
Submit death, identity and estate-authority documents plus lawful balance instructions.
boundary: Requirements and balance options vary by PayPal entity and country. Do not impersonate the account holder.

label: Coinbase
detail: Use Executor Services; individual accounts do not name a beneficiary.
doNow: Record the account email and cover the custodial assets in estate documents; never store password, 2FA or wallet seed.
later: The claimant uses their own Coinbase account and opens Executor Services.
Upload the death, probate, ID and signed transfer instructions requested by Coinbase.
boundary: Estate documents or applicable succession law determine ownership; Coinbase reviews and transfers custodial assets.

label: Binance
detail: Start an inheritance case with the exact regional Binance entity.
doNow: Record whether the account is Binance.com, Binance.US or another regional entity.
Include custodial exchange assets in estate documents; keep self-custody wallets and seeds separate.
later: An executor or beneficiary starts a case with official support for the correct entity.
Provide the identity, death and estate-authority documents that entity requests.
requirements: Exact Binance entity and account locator
boundary: No public global Binance Legacy Contact switch was verified. This is an inheritance/support application, not permission to sign in as the deceased user.
